# T3 Code

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code)), [web app](https://app.t3.codes) and [Electron-based desktop app](https://t3.codes).

Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

## "Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

## Installation

> [!WARNING]
> T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, and fx. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:
>
> - Codex: install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`
> - Claude: install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`
> - Cursor: install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli) and run `agent login`
> - Grok Build: install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli) and run `grok login`
> - OpenCode: install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and run `opencode auth login`
> - Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use **Install Antigravity** and **Sign in with Google**. No CLI is required.
> - fx: install [fx](https://fx.sh) and run `fx login` on the machine running the T3 Code server ([setup guide](./docs/user/providers-fx.md))

### Command line

```bash
curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then run `t3` to start the server and open the local web app. `t3 service install` keeps it running in the background, `t3 update` moves to a newer release, and `t3 --help` has the full reference.

To try it once without installing, run `npx t3@latest` instead.

### Desktop app

Install the latest version of the desktop app from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), or from your favorite package registry:

#### Windows (`winget`)

```bash
winget install T3Tools.T3Code
```

#### Windows (`scoop`)

```bash
scoop install extras/t3code
```

#### macOS (Homebrew)

```bash
brew install --cask t3-code
```

#### Debian, Ubuntu (`.deb`)

Download the `.deb` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), then:

```bash
sudo apt install ./T3-Code-*.deb
```

#### Arch Linux (AUR)

Stable:

```bash
yay -S t3code-bin
```

Nightly:

```bash
yay -S t3code-nightly-bin
```

The AUR packaging is maintained in this repository under [`packaging/aur`](./packaging/aur).

#### Nix (nixpkgs)

```bash
nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code
```

The package is maintained in [nixpkgs](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/tree/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/t3/t3code)
and includes the desktop app (`t3code-desktop`) and the `t3` command.
See [Nix installation](./docs/user/install.md#nix-nixpkgs) for NixOS configuration and updates.

## Some notes

We are very very early in this project. Expect bugs.

We are (mostly) not accepting contributions yet. Small fixes may be considered. Big features will not be.

## Documentation

Full docs live in [docs/](./docs). There's no docs site yet.

- [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md)
- [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md)
- [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](./docs/user/keybindings.md)
- [Project settings](./docs/user/project-settings.md)
- [Appearance preferences](./docs/user/appearance.md)
- [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md)
- [Connect Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT and other agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md)
- [Keeping app and server in sync](./docs/user/updating.md)
- [Source control integrations](./docs/user/source-control.md)
- Multiple accounts: [Codex](./docs/user/providers-codex.md) · [Claude](./docs/user/providers-claude.md)
- [Run T3 Code as a background service](./docs/user/background-service.md)

Building from source? Start at [docs/internals/overview.md](./docs/internals/overview.md).

## If you REALLY want to contribute still.... read this first

### Install `vp`

T3 Code uses Vite+ so you'll need to install the global `vp` command-line tool.

#### macOS / Linux

```bash
curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash
```

#### Windows

```bash
irm https://vite.plus/ps1 | iex
```

Checkout their getting started guide for more information: https://viteplus.dev/guide/

### Install dependencies

```bash
vp i
```

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before reporting a bug or opening a PR.

Have a feature request? Start an [Ideas discussion](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas).

Need support? Join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv).

# OpenBot **The AI assistant your company can actually own.** Same shape as ChatGPT, Claude or Grok, with one difference that matters: it runs on your infrastructure and you can change anything about it. Any agent stack, through AG-UI. Each coworker gets a real browser with its own logins, its own files, and only the tools you grant. Every action decided before it happens and recorded after. [**Talk to an engineer**](https://copilotkit.ai/talk-to-an-engineer?ref=openbot_readme) · [**Have us build it with you**](https://copilotkit.ai/talk-to-an-engineer?ref=openbot_readme) · [**copilotkit.ai/openbot**](https://copilotkit.ai/openbot) · [**Quick start**](#quick-start) · [**Docs**](docs/README.md) [![CI](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openbot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openbot/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![security](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openbot/actions/workflows/security_zizmor.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openbot/actions/workflows/security_zizmor.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE) ![Beta](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-beta-yellow.svg) [![GitHub Trending: #5 Repository Of The Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/repositories/175080)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/175080) [![Trendshift: #3 Repository Of The Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/trendshift/repositories/175080/daily)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/175080)
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/535ef7ee-1631-4a69-b839-564c56cf90b4
Bring any AG-UI agent, written on a framework or by hand, and it arrives as a coworker with a channel of its own. Watch it work on its own screen, take the wheel when it reaches something it should not do alone, then hand it back. It answers with components rather than only prose, and the whole thing runs on your own machine.
> **A template, not a product.** OpenBot is meant to be cloned and made your own. There is no hosted version to sign up for, and nothing here is published as a package to depend on: every workspace in this repository is private. You take the repository, replace the example tenant package under `examples/` with your own coworkers, channels and skills, and run it. Everything below describes a starting point, not a finished thing somebody operates for you. > **Beta, and under active development.** OpenBot is early. Expect rough edges and bugs, and expect things to move. Issues and pull requests are welcome. > **Runs on your machine.** Everything below is written for a laptop. `.env.example` carries `OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true`, which admits every request as one administrator, so a fresh clone reaches the product without registering an OAuth client first. [Sign-in](#sign-in) turns that off, and is required before anybody else can reach the deployment. > **We can build this for you, or with you, at your company.** Our engineers will stand OpenBot up > inside your infrastructure, customize it into something that looks like your own product, and hand it > back to you to keep changing. [**Start the conversation**](https://copilotkit.ai/talk-to-an-engineer?ref=openbot_readme). > > In the meantime, run all of it on your laptop, Intelligence included: CopilotKit's free Developer plan > covers [running Intelligence locally](#intelligence-on-your-own-machine) in Docker on a Mac. ## What it is An agent platform that runs inside your own infrastructure. Docker Compose brings up every part of it, the data sits in your PostgreSQL, and the model is yours to choose: no model ships in the box, and an administrator supplies the credential, which is encrypted at rest and never logged. A deployment starts with two coworkers, and they are configuration rather than code: **General Assistant** for everyday work and **Knowledge** for company questions. A **Risk Analyst** joins them once its endpoint is configured, and ten more wait in `examples/fintech/catalog/`, each doing one job — reading an expense claim against the policy as written, turning a meeting note into the follow-ups actually in it, drafting release notes from what shipped, triaging a ticket, answering a new starter from the handbook, writing a brief that names what it could not find, writing up an interview, handing an on-call shift over, assembling what is known before a renewal, and grouping customer feedback into themes it can cite. Copy one into `examples/fintech/agents/` to add it, write your own there or in `agents.yaml`, or make one from `/bots` in the UI. Anything a Bot does to a computer, a file, an MCP server or a component goes through one gateway that decides and records it. That is the difference between an agent that can use your tools and an agent you can let near them. More at [copilotkit.ai/openbot](https://copilotkit.ai/openbot). ## Built on AG-UI A Bot is any endpoint speaking [AG-UI](https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui), the open protocol for agent-to-user interaction, so OpenBot is not tied to a framework and neither are you. Agents built with LangGraph, Mastra, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, Google ADK or written by hand all arrive the same way, and the governance rides the protocol rather than the framework. ## Requirements - Docker, for PostgreSQL and the shipped Bots. - [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4+, for the app, the API server and the tests (some tests fail on 1.3). - A CopilotKit Intelligence project and license. A free plan is available, and Intelligence can be self-hosted. - A model key. The proof-of-concept Bot uses OpenAI; the LangGraph Bot can use OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google. ## Quick start > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Paste [`prompt.txt`](prompt.txt) into it first. It carries the > same steps as below plus the things that are easy to get wrong: which of the blank keys in > `.env.example` are actually yours to fill (the CopilotKit key and a model key), which the start > script fills for you, and what each start-up refusal means. Every claim in it is checked against > this repository. 1. Create `.env`: ```sh cp .env.example .env bun install ``` 2. Connect a fresh managed Intelligence project: ```sh npx --yes copilotkit@latest login npx --yes copilotkit@latest project select bun scripts/setup-learning.ts ``` The helper provisions the selected project's runtime key, creates or reuses its `openbot` Learning container, then writes both settings to `.env`. It preserves custom container assignments and never replaces an existing OpenBot key; with one set, it only creates `openbot` in that key's project if it is missing. For fresh self-hosted setup, set `INTELLIGENCE_API_URL` to that deployment's HTTPS API origin (or `http://localhost` for a local one) and run the helper without the two `npx` commands. It opens an isolated Chrome or Edge window for your usual sign-in and project choice; install either browser first. For CLI-managed local evaluation installs, it discovers the matching dashboard with the newest installed or cached CopilotKit CLI and uses that dashboard for login and session requests. Discovery runs offline with Bun, without downloading the CLI or requiring `npx` on your PATH. If no CLI is available, manually hosted deployments use their API origin for sign-in. Complete the local auth approval shown in the browser when prompted. The runtime API URL stays unchanged. It writes the API URL, the key and the container, not `INTELLIGENCE_GATEWAY_WS_URL`, so set that one to the same deployment yourself. Once `openbot` exists, the server assigns it as the default by itself unless [Admin → Automatic Learning](docs/automatic-learning.md) has a saved setting. Managed Intelligence needs no separate licence token. 3. Fill the remaining required values: - `OPENAI_API_KEY` Keep the managed Intelligence URLs from `.env.example` unless you run Intelligence yourself. The example `KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is public and fine locally; generate your own with: ```sh openssl rand -base64 32 ``` 4. Run: ```sh bash scripts/start.sh ``` 5. Open . `scripts/start.sh` starts Docker services, applies migrations, starts the API server on port 3001, starts the routine worker, starts the app on port 3010, and checks that the services answer their own health routes before printing next steps. `scripts/stop.sh` takes the same things down, including each Bot's computer, which compose does not own; `--keep-computers` leaves the computers running. Nothing is deleted: the database, the Bots' files and their browser profiles are volumes. ### Intelligence on your own machine To try Intelligence on one Mac instead of the managed service, follow [Evaluate Intelligence locally](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/intelligence/self-hosting-local). The free [Developer plan](https://www.copilotkit.ai/pricing) qualifies. The local licence lasts 30 days and `npx copilotkit@latest local renew` renews it as often as you need, while your account is in good standing. It is a preview for macOS with Docker Desktop, not a production installation. Run its `npx copilotkit@latest local connect` from the OpenBot root, where `.env` is. That command writes `INTELLIGENCE_API_URL`, `INTELLIGENCE_GATEWAY_WS_URL` and `CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY` to `.env`. OpenBot reads those settings directly; no key copying or renaming is needed. `INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY` remains supported for older configurations. When both are set, the non-empty CLI key takes precedence so reconnecting uses the new project's key. To give the Bots a Learning container on that stack, see [Automatic Learning](docs/automatic-learning.md). ## Deploy it One image carries the app, the API, the browser the Bots drive, and optionally PostgreSQL. Same `.env`, no Kubernetes. ```sh # The published image. Nothing to clone and nothing to build. docker run -p 3001:3001 --env-file .env \ -e EMBEDDED_POSTGRES=on -v openbot-data:/var/lib/postgresql \ ghcr.io/copilotkit/openbot:latest # Or the tree you have in front of you. docker build -t openbot . docker run -p 3001:3001 --env-file .env \ -e EMBEDDED_POSTGRES=on -v openbot-data:/var/lib/postgresql openbot ``` Everything is on 3001 here, the app included, rather than the 3010 the clone uses. `latest` is the most recent release and a version tag such as `:v0.0.9` pins one. Leave `EMBEDDED_POSTGRES` off and set `DATABASE_URL` to point at a database you already run. [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md) has the minimum sizes, the platform notes, and how it behaves behind more than one replica. ## Try it - Open `/bot` and ask: `Open news.ycombinator.com and tell me the top story.` - Ask the Bot to fill out , then inspect `/admin/audit`. - Open `/admin/boundaries`, add a deny rule or preset, and retry the same browser action. - Create a Bot from `/bots`, give it a standing role, and start a channel with it. ## Main surfaces | Route | Purpose | | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `/` | Start and browse channels. | | `/channel/new`

Persistent memory compression system built for Claude Code.


Quick Start • How It Works • Search Tools • Documentation • Configuration • Troubleshooting • License

Claude-Mem seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect.

--- ## Quick Start Install claude-mem for Grok Bot: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. **Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice):** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Disable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false`. Install with a single command: ```bash npx claude-mem install ``` The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the **claude-mem observer** with a **30 Day Free Trial**: memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider — the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Or install for OpenCode: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide opencode ``` This works with OpenCode 1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2. Restart OpenCode after installing. Or install for **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide t3code ``` The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal. Or install for Antigravity CLI ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity ``` Or install for OMP (Oh My Pi): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide omp ``` Or install the native Pi extension or DeepSeek Harness plugin: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide pi npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui ``` Pi and DeepSeek Harness use the worker runtime. See [native harness setup](docs/native-harness-integrations.md) for capture, recall, and troubleshooting. Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem /plugin install claude-mem ``` Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions. > **Note:** Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but `npm install -g claude-mem` installs the **SDK/library only** — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via `npx claude-mem install` or the `/plugin` commands above. ### 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) gateways with a single command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash ``` The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the [OpenClaw Integration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/openclaw-integration) for details. **Key Features:** - 🧠 **Persistent Memory** - Context survives across sessions - 📊 **Progressive Disclosure** - Layered memory retrieval with token cost visibility - 🔍 **Smart Search (Default)** - Query your project history with the three-step mem-search skill - 🖥️ **Local My Work** - Live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. [Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/my-work). Memory, sessions and settings remain at `/viewer`. - 👥 **TeamBrain** - An optional shared workspace beside My Work, with real team work lists, member attribution and linked findings. Each person chooses what to share; personal requests and review notes stay separate. [Set up a team](https://cmem.ai/teambrain/start). - 💻 **Claude Desktop Skill** - Search memory from Claude Desktop conversations - 🔒 **Privacy Control** - Use `` tags to exclude sensitive content from storage - 🖼️ **Screenshots (opt-in, off by default)** - Keep converted copies of tool screenshots under `~/.claude-mem/media-v1/`, upload them to cmem.ai only when Cloud Sync is on, and send them to the observer model only when image inference is separately enabled ([details](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration#screenshots-and-images-opt-in)) - ⚙️ **Context Configuration** - Fine-grained control over what context gets injected - 🤖 **Automatic Operation** - No manual intervention required - 🔗 **Citations** - Reference past observations with IDs through the worker API or view all in the web viewer --- ## Documentation 📚 **[View Full Documentation](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/)** - Browse on official website ### Getting Started - **[Installation Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/installation)** - Quick start & advanced installation - **[Usage Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/getting-started)** - How Claude-Mem works automatically - **[Search Tools](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools)** - Query your project history with natural language - **[Cloud Sync](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/cloud-sync)** - Back up your memories to cmem.ai — no daemon, the worker syncs on write ### Best Practices - **[Context Engineering](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/context-engineering)** - AI agent context optimization principles - **[Progressive Disclosure](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/progressive-disclosure)** - Philosophy behind Claude-Mem's context priming strategy ### Architecture - **[Overview](htt

# Hex

Hex is local voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux. Hold a key, speak, and
it pastes.

## How it works

- hold the shortcut, speak, then let go
- Hex transcribes on your device and pastes into whatever app you're in
- the first run downloads a speech model; after that nothing leaves your machine
- experimental features live in Labs, at the bottom of the sidebar

## Downloads

Stable is the current release. Dev is the newest build of `dev` and updates
itself from the dev channel.

| Platform | Stable | Dev |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/macos-arm64-dmg) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/macos-arm64-dmg) |
| Windows x64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-x64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-x64-setup) |
| Windows ARM64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-arm64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-arm64-setup) |
| Linux x86_64 | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64) | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64) |
| Linux x86_64 (Debian, Ubuntu) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64-deb) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64-deb) |

# Handy [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-%235865F2.svg?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.com/invite/WVBeWsNXK4) **A free, open source, and extensible speech-to-text application that works completely offline.** Handy is a cross-platform desktop application that provides simple, privacy-focused speech transcription. Press a shortcut, speak, and have your words appear in any text field. This happens on your own computer without sending any information to the cloud. ## Why Handy? Handy was created to fill the gap for a truly open source, extensible speech-to-text tool. As stated on [handy.computer](https://handy.computer): - **Free**: Accessibility tooling belongs in everyone's hands, not behind a paywall - **Open Source**: Together we can build further. Extend Handy for yourself and contribute to something bigger - **Private**: Your voice stays on your computer. Get transcriptions without sending audio to the cloud - **Simple**: One tool, one job. Transcribe what you say and put it into a text box ## How It Works 1. **Press** a configurable keyboard shortcut: hold it to record and release to stop, or tap it to toggle recording on and off (Hold-only and Toggle-only modes are also available) 2. **Speak** your words while the shortcut is active 3. **Release** and Handy processes your speech using Whisper 4. **Get** your transcribed text pasted directly into whatever app you're using The process is entirely local: - Silence is filtered using VAD (Voice Activity Detection) with Silero - Transcription uses your choice of models: - **Whisper models** (Small/Medium/Turbo/Large) with GPU acceleration when available - **Parakeet V3** - CPU-optimized model with excellent performance and automatic language detection - Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux ## Quick Start ### Installation 1. Download the latest release from the [releases page](https://github.com/cjpais/Handy/releases) or the [website](https://handy.computer) - **macOS**: Also available via [Homebrew cask](https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/handy): `brew install --cask handy` - **Windows**: Also available via [winget](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs): `winget install cjpais.Handy` \ **Note:** The Homebrew cask and winget package are not maintained by the Handy developers. - **Debian/Ubuntu**: Install the downloaded `.deb` with APT so required dependencies are installed automatically: ```bash sudo apt install ./Handy_*.deb ``` Do not use `dpkg -i` unless the dependencies are already installed. If you already used it, run `sudo apt --fix-broken install`. 2. Install the application 3. Launch Handy and grant necessary system permissions (microphone, accessibility) 4. Configure your preferred keyboard shortcuts in Settings 5. Start transcribing! ### Development Setup For detailed build instructions including platform-specific requirements, see [BUILD.md](BUILD.md). ## Sponsors
We're grateful for the support of our sponsors who help make Handy possible:

                    
## Integrations Control Handy from [Raycast](https://www.raycast.com) — start/stop recording, browse transcript history, manage dictionary, switch models and languages. [Source](https://github.com/mattiacolombomc/raycast-handy) · by [@mattiacolombomc](https://github.com/mattiacolombomc) ### Debug Mode Handy includes an advanced debug mode for development and troubleshooting. Access it by pressing: - **macOS**: `Cmd+Shift+D` - **Windows/Linux**: `Ctrl+Shift+D` ### CLI Parameters Handy supports command-line flags for controlling a running instance and customizing startup behavior. These work on all platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux). Largely this is a beta feature. **Remote control flags** (sent to an already-running instance via the single-instance plugin): ```bash handy --toggle-transcription # Toggle recording on/off handy --toggle-post-process # Toggle recording with post-processing on/off handy --cancel # Cancel the current operation ``` **Startup flags:** ```bash handy --start-hidden # Start without showing the main window handy --no-tray # Start without the system tray icon handy --debug # Enable debug mode with verbose logging handy --help # Show all available flags ``` Flags can be combined for autostart scenarios: ```bash handy --start-hidden --no-tray ``` > **macOS tip:** When Handy is installed as an app bundle, invoke the binary directly: > > ```bash > /Applications/Handy.app/Contents/MacOS/Handy --toggle-transcription > ``` ## Known Issues & Current Limitations This project is actively being developed and has some [known issues](https://github.com/cjpais/Handy/issues). We believe in transparency about the current state: ### Bluetooth Headset Microphones (macOS) Using a Bluetooth headset microphone on macOS may temporarily reduce playback quality or volume while recording because Bluetooth switches to bidirectional audio. Keep your headphones as the output device and select your Mac's built-in or an external microphone in Handy to avoid this. ### fn and Globe Key Shortcuts (macOS) Shortcuts that include the `fn` (Globe) key **only work on Apple keyboards** — your Mac's built-in keyboard or an Apple external keyboard. They will never trigger on a third-party keyboard, even while it is connected to the same Mac. This is a hardware limitation rather than a Handy bug. `fn` is not part of the standard USB HID keyboard specification: Apple reports it through a vendor-specific usage that macOS honors only from Apple devices, while third-party keyboards handle their `Fn` key entirely in firmware and send nothing to the computer. There is no event for Handy to listen for. If you switch between a MacBook keyboard and an external one, pick a shortcut built from standard modifiers (`ctrl`, `option`, `shift`, `command`) or a regular key instead. ### Linux Notes **Text Input Tools:** For reliable text input on Linux, install the appropriate tool for your display server: | Display Server | Recommended Tool | Install Command | | -------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | X11 | `xdotool` | `sudo apt install xdotool` | | Wayland | `wtype` | `sudo apt install wtype` | | Both | `dotool` | `sudo apt install dotool` (requires `input` group) | - **X11**: Install `xdotool` for both direct typing and clipboard paste shortcuts - **Ubuntu 26.04**: Has Wayland display server by default. `wtype` does not work, you need to install `ydotool` and configure systemd as described [here](https://github.com/cjpais/Handy/pull/557#issuecomment-3781249267). - **Wayland**: Install `wtype` (preferred) or `dotool` for text input to work correctly - **dotool setup**: Requires adding your user to the `input` group: `sudo usermod -aG input $USER` (then log out and back in) Without these tools, Handy falls back to enigo which may have limited compatibility, especially on Wayland. **Wayland Support (Linux):** - Limited support for Wayland display server - Requires [`wtype`](https://github.com/atx/wtype) or [`dotool`](https://sr.ht/~geb/dotool/) for text input to work correctly (see [Linux Notes](#linux-notes) below for installation) **Other Notes:** - **Runtime library dependency (`libgtk-layer-shell.so.0`)**: - Handy links `gtk-layer-shell` on Linux. If startup fails with `error while loading shared libraries: libgtk-layer-shell.so.0`, install the runtime package for your distro: | Distro | Package to install | Example command | | ------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------- | | Ubuntu/Debian | `libgtk-layer-shell0` | `sudo apt install libgtk-layer-shell0` | | Fedora/RHEL | `gtk-layer-shell` | `sudo dnf install gtk-layer-shell` | | Arch Linux | `gtk-layer-shell` | `sudo pacman -S gtk-layer-shell` | - For building from source on Ubuntu/Debian, you may also need `libgtk-layer-shell-dev`. - The recording overlay is disabled by default on Linux (`Overlay Position: None`) because certain compositors treat it as the active window. When the overlay is visible it can steal focus, which prevents Handy from pasting back into the application that triggered transcription. If you enable the overlay anyway, be aware that clipboard-based pasting might fail or end up in the wrong window. - Handy disables the WebKit DMA-BUF renderer by default on Linux, but preserves explicit `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` values. For rendering workarounds, see [Troubleshooting → Linux Startup Crashes or Instability](#linux-startup-crashes-or-instability). - If Handy fails to start reliably on Linux, see [Troubleshooting → Linux Startup Crashes or Instability](#linux-startup-crashes-or-instability). - **Global keyboard shortcuts (Wayland):** On Wayland, system-level shortcuts must be configured through your desktop environment or window manager. Use the [CLI flags](#cli-parameters) as the command for your custom shortcut. **GNOME:** 1. Open **Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > Custom Shortcuts** 2. Click the **+** button to add a new shortcut 3. Set the **Name** to `Toggle Handy Transcription` 4. Set the **Command** to `handy --toggle-transcription` 5. Click **Set Shortcut** and press your desired key combination (e.g., `Super+O`) **KDE Plasma:** 1. Open **System Settings > Shortcuts > Custom Shortcuts** 2. Click **Edit > New > Global Shortcut > Command/URL** 3. Name it `Toggle Handy Transcription` 4. In the **Trigger** tab, set your desired key combination 5. In the **Action** tab, set the command to `handy --toggle-transcription` **Sway / i3:** Add to your config file (`~/.config/sway/config` or `~/.config/i3/config`): ```ini bindsym $mod+o exec handy --toggle-transcription ``` **Hyprland:** Add to your config file (`~/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf`): ```ini bind = $mainMod, O, exec, handy --toggle-transcription ``` - You can also trigger Handy externally via Unix signals or the CLI flags, which lets Wayland window managers or other hotkey daemons keep ownership of keybindings: | Action | Trigger | | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | | Toggle transcription | `pkill -USR2 -n handy` or `handy --toggle-transcription` | | Toggle transcription with post-processing | `handy --toggle-post-process` | Example Sway config: ```ini bindsym $mod+o exec pkill -USR2 -n handy bindsym $mod+p exec handy --toggle-post-process ``` `pkill` here simply delivers the signal—it does not terminate the process. > **Behavio

# Horizon Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, rewritten in Rust. Same worlds, same rules, same terrain, checked against the Java game by more than 300 differential harnesses. Free, open source and unofficial. > Not an official Minecraft product, nor approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft. Horizon contains no Minecraft code, assets or data: you need your own copy of Java Edition 26.3. ## Download Get **the Horizon launcher** from [playhorizon.dev](https://playhorizon.dev) or [the launcher releases](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/releases?q=launcher-v&expanded=true) (Linux x86-64, macOS on Apple Silicon, macOS on Intel from the next Nightly, Windows x64). It installs and updates the game, prepares its files from your copy of Minecraft, and updates itself. **You need** a Microsoft account that owns Java Edition ([why](docs/microsoft-account.md)) and a GPU with Vulkan or OpenGL 3.3 (Linux), Vulkan or DirectX 12 (Windows), or a Mac (Apple Silicon, or Intel from the next Nightly). An existing Minecraft install (official launcher, Prism, MultiMC...) is reused; without one, Play downloads 26.3 from Mojang for your account. Step by step: [Install and first launch](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/install).
## What works today - **The game:** vanilla world generation, mobs, villagers, raids, redstone, every command, the HUD and the recipe book, on vanilla saves. Worlds from 1.8 to 26.2 are upgraded. [Status](#project-status). - **Extras:** new menus, graphics presets, distant terrain up to 1024 chunks, controllers, zoom, minimap and more, off by default where they change the vanilla look. [Settings](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/settings). - **Packs:** resource packs, and data packs with functions, predicates, item modifiers and world generation. - **Multiplayer:** invite friends with a code, Open to LAN, join servers (online mode included). [Multiplayer](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/multiplayer). - **Mods:** content mods (blocks, items, data) and native Rust mods, built by the launcher with nothing to install. Java mod jars do not run. [Mods](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/mods). In the Rust client, with vanilla assets and no mods or shaders:
## Host a server The launcher's **Servers** page creates, starts, backs up and updates a server, and invites friends over Tailscale. On a VPS, `horizon-server` installs with one command and needs no Java. [Host a server](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/hosting) ([reference](docs/hosting.md)). ## Modpacks The launcher imports Modrinth and CurseForge packs and plays the mods Horizon can carry over: today, content mods made of data and assets, not Java code. [Modpacks](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/modpacks). ## Agent control AI agents and scripts can play Horizon. `horizon-ctl`, shipped with the game, reads its state as JSON and acts like a player; `horizon-ctl mcp` serves the same commands over MCP. ```sh horizon-ctl launch --world Survival --seed 5 --wait # finds the version the launcher installed horizon-ctl state # position, health, food, target, screen... horizon-ctl find-block birch_log # the nearest logs horizon-ctl goto -0.5 65 -2.5 --near 2.5 # walks there along a path horizon-ctl break -1 65 -3 # mines it; replies with the drops horizon-ctl open-inventory && horizon-ctl click-slot 0 # menus: slots, buttons by label, text fields ``` Commands block until done and reply with the result; `horizon-ctl help` lists them all. [Agent control](docs/native-client.md#agent-control-horizon-ctl-and-mcp). ## Build from source Needs Rust 1.90+, Python 3.10+, JDK 25, and on Linux `libasound2-dev libudev-dev`. `horizon-prepare` builds the game's resources from **your own copy** of Java Edition 26.3 (checked against `research-lock.json`) and never downloads it: 1. **Client:** play 26.3 once in the official launcher. Horizon reads `~/.minecraft` (or `--minecraft-dir` / `HORIZON_MINECRAFT_DIR`). 2. **Server jar:** the 26.3 server jar (`downloads.server.url` in `versions/26.3/26.3.json`), passed once with `--server-jar` or `HORIZON_SERVER_JAR`. ```sh git clone https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon.git cd horizon cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- --prepare --server-jar ~/Downloads/server.jar # needs JDK 25 cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- sounds # optional: sounds from your launcher install cargo run --release -p horizon-client ``` Prepared files land in the gitignored `.local/`: never commit or share them. Options, controls and architecture: [the native client guide](docs/native-client.md); all developer docs: [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). ## Roadmap What is in progress, what comes next and where to help: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), or [playhorizon.dev/hub](https://playhorizon.dev/hub) with the work board and what shipped. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome: read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) (vanilla first, small pull requests). Questions: [Discord](https://discord.gg/playhorizon). Before a pull request, run the self-check and paste its output: ```sh git config core.hooksPath .githooks python3 tools/pr_ready.py ``` It runs rustfmt, clippy, the touched crates' tests, the Python tests, the public-tree check and the vanilla harnesses your change affects. Never commit game files, decompiled source or prepared resources. ## Project status **Player-visible gaps: 833 open** of the 833 the [port ledger](tools/port_ledger.py) found, reading every vanilla 26.3 method against Horizon's code: vanilla behaviour a player would notice that Horizon doesn't have yet. By area: Screens, HUD and client packets [197](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3518); Entity and block rendering, models [129](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3519); Animals [110](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3512); Server and players on the server [106](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3520); Blocks, redstone and fluids [86](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3516); Entities, projectiles, vehicles and decorations [64](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3514); Monsters and bosses [53](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3513); Mob AI, villagers and raids [35](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3521); World, world generation and saves [32](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3517); Items, enchantments and inventories [21](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3515). This number goes down as gaps close (`tools/parity_gaps.py`); the harness results below say that what is tested matches. The table is the project's own audit: every subsystem matches vanilla in every harness that compares it. 100% means 100% of what the harnesses compare, not that nothing else differs. ### Java parity: 100% Scores: 0 (absent), 0.25 (started), 0.5 (playable, major features missing), 0.75 (mostly complete) or 1 (complete and verified by differential tests); the percentage is their average. Turn videos into transparent PNG animation frames, or create new characters and motion with the optional built-in AI image / video generation. **Local extraction, background removal, alignment, and trimming are free and require no login or credits. Check the source silhouette and motion first. If you need source material, create a character in Image Generation, then use that image as the first frame in Video Generation. See the AI setup options below. #### 2. You can hide and restore unwanted frames in steps 02 / 03. Re-extracting frames invalidates older downstream results. Once the model is ready, local processing works offline. After Step 03, choose the **magic wand or eraser at the preview’s bottom right** to pause and retouch the current frame in place. Tool settings appear at the top, with brief instructions inside the preview. Click to select, Shift-click to add, and Delete to remove; left-drag to erase. Scroll to zoom, middle-drag to pan, and use Space for playback. The preview keeps its background, zoom and pan; background switching remains available. Cancel discards unsaved changes. Edits affect only this frame in Step 03. Re-running Step 03 replaces manual edits. Wand deletion fully clears the selection and feathers outward into neighboring pixels; with feathering set to 0, only selected pixels are cleared. Restore Initial Version returns the current frame to this processing run’s Step 03 output before manual edits, across saves and restarts. Restoration can be undone and requires Save to update the output. If older backups do not identify their processing step, restoration stays disabled until Step 03 is reprocessed to establish a verified baseline. #### 3. Open the output directory from the results to get the PNG sequence and related JSON. Keep `_audio_timeline.json` and audio files when present. details.readme:
# Moono [English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) An unofficial, super fast, super sussy replacement for the Unity layer of Oxygen Not Included, artisanally crafted by Claude. On a late-game colony the game runs at about 8× the original's frame rate ([Performance](#performance)).

I did this mostly for fun, to see how far Oxygen Not Included's performance can go on a modern .NET runtime (CoreCLR). I've had the idea for a while, but none of the existing C# renderers sparked joy. When [BRUTAL](https://github.com/ahwootech/BRUTAL) went open source, it seemed like a good excuse to try a sexy new toy. Moono runs Klei's original DLLs, patched at load where Mono and .NET [differ](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Everything they need from Unity is reimplemented here. ## Setup You need your own copy of the game on Steam, on Linux or Windows (no macOS). Epic Games Store and WeGame (China) are not currently supported. Because this replaces the engine rather than patching the game, it can't ship as an ordinary Harmony mod. Instead, a setup script hooks it into the game's Steam launch options, so you still start the game from Steam as usual. ### Easy installation 1. Download the latest release from the [releases page](https://github.com/tigin-backwards/oni-moono/releases/latest): `oni-moono-…-windows-x64.zip` or `oni-moono-…-linux-x64.tar.gz`, and extract it anywhere. (Or clone this repository; the setup then builds the player itself, installing the .NET SDK for your user if you don't have it.) 2. Run the setup script in the extracted `oni-moono` folder: - Windows: double-click `setup.cmd` (it runs `setup.ps1` and keeps the window open) - Linux: `./setup.sh` It finds your Oxygen Not Included install through Steam, and prints one line for the game's launch options, and puts it on your clipboard where it can. 3. In Steam, right-click Oxygen Not Included → Properties → Launch Options, and paste that line. ![Steam's Properties dialog with the Launch Options box](docs/images/steam-launch-options.png) Then press Play in Steam as usual. The optional tweaks (below) are chosen in the game: **Moono Tweaks** on the main menu, under Mods. To update, get the new version and run the setup again; the launch options stay the same, and so do your tweak choices. To go back to the original game, clear the launch options. On Linux, Steam installed as a Flatpak or a snap runs games in a sandbox that can't see most of your home folder; the setup notices and installs the player inside the sandbox's own folder. (Snap is tested; Flatpak isn't yet.) You'll need an OpenGL 4.5 graphics driver. The game uses your normal Steam account, DLCs, saves, settings and mods. ### Manual installation The setup script (see above) is the easiest installation on most systems. If you want more control, need to customize the installation, or run a sandboxed environment and prefer not to run a script outside of that, follow these manual steps. They don't include instructions on how to build the player from scratch; see the setup scripts for the build steps, or [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).
Linux The example paths match those used by `setup.sh`, with `~/Downloads/oni-moono/` as the location of the downloaded and extracted files. You can choose different paths, but update them consistently in the commands and Steam launch options below. 1. **Locate the game folder.** It must contain `OxygenNotIncluded` and `OxygenNotIncluded_Data/Managed`. Common Steam library locations include: - Default Steam: `~/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/OxygenNotIncluded` or `~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/OxygenNotIncluded` - Snap Steam: `~/snap/steam/common/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/OxygenNotIncluded` - Flatpak Steam: `~/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/OxygenNotIncluded` If the game is in another Steam library, use that library's `steamapps/common/OxygenNotIncluded` folder instead. Confirm that `OxygenNotIncluded` is the Linux executable; a Windows installation via compatibility tools (Proton) will not work. 2. **Place the player where Steam can access it.** In the downloaded archive, the `player` folder should contain the `OniMoono` executable and its accompanying files. (The `rm -rf` commands in the following examples remove a previous `player` folder, in case you are updating. Check the path before running them, or use your file manager instead.) For a regular Steam installation, you can leave the `player` folder where you extracted the archive (`setup.sh` does so), or copy it somewhere convenient: ```bash # Default Steam mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin/oni-moono" rm -rf "$HOME/.local/bin/oni-moono/player" cp -rp "$HOME/Downloads/oni-moono/player" "$HOME/.local/bin/oni-moono/player" ``` Snap and Flatpak Steam run in sandboxes and may not be able to access files elsewhere in your home folder. Copy the player into Steam's sandbox-visible location: ```bash # Snap Steam mkdir -p "$HOME/snap/steam/common/oni-moono" rm -rf "$HOME/snap/steam/common/oni-moono/player" cp -rp "$HOME/Downloads/oni-moono/player" "$HOME/snap/steam/common/oni-moono/player" ``` ```bash # Flatpak Steam mkdir -p "$HOME/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/data/oni-moono" rm -rf "$HOME/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/data/oni-moono/player" cp -rp "$HOME/Downloads/oni-moono/player" \ "$HOME/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/data/oni-moono/player" ``` 3. **Check the executable bit.** The player binary `OniMoono` must be executable. Set it if needed, using the path where you placed the player: ```bash chmod +x "$HOME/.local/bin/oni-moono/player/OniMoono" ``` For Snap or Flatpak, use the corresponding paths above. Check that the file exists and is executable with `ls -l`. 4. **Set Steam's launch options.** In Steam, right-click Oxygen Not Included → Properties → Launch Options. Enter one line, replacing the example path with the full path to your player: ```text "/home/your-username/.local/bin/oni-moono/player/OniMoono" -- %command% ``` For Snap, the executable path is typically: ```text "/home/your-username/snap/steam/common/oni-moono/player/OniMoono" -- %command% ``` For Flatpak, it is typically: ```text "/home/your-username/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/data/oni-moono/player/OniMoono" -- %command% ``` Replace `/home/your-username` with your actual home folder path. Do not use a literal `~` or `$HOME` in the launch options. Keep the quotes around the executable path, especially if it contains spaces. Press Play in Steam. If the game does not start, check that the launch options path matches the player's actual location, `OniMoono` has its execute bit set, and the game folder contains the Linux build. If that doesn't help, launch Steam from a terminal and watch the output for a hint after clicking Play. For updates, download the new release archive and repeat the steps, replacing the `player` folder. To remove Moono and return to the original game, remove the `player` folder from where you put it, and clear the launch options in Steam.
Windows 1. **Place the player.** In the downloaded archive, the `player` folder contains `OniMoono.exe` and its accompanying files. Copy it to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\oni-moono\player`, the location `setup.ps1` uses (paste `%LOCALAPPDATA%` into Explorer's address bar to open it). You can choose a different folder, but with this one, running the setup later keeps the same launch options. In case you are updating, remove the previous `player` folder first. 2. **Set Steam's launch options.** In Steam, right-click Oxygen Not Included → Properties → Launch Options. Enter one line, replacing the example path with the full path to your player: ```text "C:\Users\your-username\AppData\Local\oni-moono\player\OniMoono.exe" -- %command% ``` Replace `C:\Users\your-username` with your actual user folder path. Do not use `%LOCALAPPDATA%` in the launch options. Keep the quotes around the executable path. Press Play in Steam. If the game does not start, check that the launch options path matches the player's actual location. For updates, download the new release archive and repeat the steps, replacing the `player` folder. To remove Moono and return to the original game, remove the `player` folder, and clear the launch options in Steam.
## Performance The biggest change is swapping the very garbage Mono runtime that Unity ships for CoreCLR. On top of that there are optimizations tuned to the way Oxygen Not Included uses the engine. On a late-game save (U57: Spaced Out with every DLC, cycle 17,000+), on Windows, on the same machine, back to back: | | Original | Moono | | |---|---|---|---| | Frame rate at speed 3 (default tweaks) | about 11 fps | about 88 fps | about 8× | | Loading the save | 2 min 22 s | about 35 s | about 4× faster | | Autosave freeze | about 26 s | about 2.3 s | about 11× shorter | | Starting the game, to the main menu (every DLC, second launch) | about 17.4 s | about 9.8 s | about 1.8× faster | How much faster it runs depends on your hardware. Moono removes the runtime's overhead, so the faster your CPU, the more of the gain you see. On slower machines, you'll get bottlenecked by other things sooner: running out of memory, or the game's C++ simulation itself, which Moono doesn't speed up (particularly on very large custom maps). Garbage-collection hitches are mostly gone: collections now run in the background, spread across every core, and their pauses are about a quarter as long. **Note:** This uses more memory compared to the original. On a mid-game colony, memory peaked at around 11GB resident compared to 7GB in the original. This is expected behavior for faster, parallel collection. U57 at speed 3: about 11 fps in the original, about 88 in Moono. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d54b5ac-8583-442c-b6ad-8ddaa31e6d6d Starting the game to the main menu, every DLC, second launch: 17.6 s in the original, 10.0 s in Moono. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb1bf869-b031-4090-86b8-1714535f36e4 An autosave on U57: the original freezes for about 26 s, Moono for about 4 s. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0534ae4-115f-4b17-b9bb-2f8c28868b89 The temperature overlay on U57, panning: about 8 fps in the original, about 50 in Moono. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0054f3c-0462-4333-955b-9ab5c8888810 2minnow, a mid-game colony, at speed 3: about 35 fps in the original, about 110 in Moono. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3106d24d-67d3-4bf3-ba23-8f8dc78910f8 For a more detailed breakdown, see [docs/PERFORMANCE.md](docs/PERFORMANCE.md). ### Tweaks Moono also speeds up some of the game's own code. Most tweaks don't change gameplay and are on by default; four do, and are off. Toggle them in **Moono Tweaks** on the main menu. Full list: [docs/TWEAKS.md](docs/TWEAKS.md). ![The main menu with the Moono Tweaks button under Mods](docs/images/main-menu.png)
